title: TekGlove
summary: TekGlove is a wearable technology platform powered by a Smart Dorsal Sensor. Its ecosystem uses hand-derived data, artificial intelligence, gesture recognition, biometrics, and connected technology to support products across healthcare, sport, productivity, rehabilitation, security, and human-computer interaction.
shortDescription: A scalable digital platform for an intelligent wearable ecosystem powered by hand-derived data and Smart Dorsal Sensor technology.

overview: TekGlove is a wearable technology platform that transforms data from the hand into useful intelligence across a growing family of connected gloves.
The project evolved from a single product website into a scalable ecosystem for six products serving healthcare, sport, rehabilitation, productivity, security, and human-computer interaction.
The digital experience needed to explain the shared Smart Dorsal Sensor architecture while giving each product a distinct purpose and identity.
contribution: Built the frontend with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Motion.
Structured the information architecture around the Smart Dorsal Sensor and a six-product wearable ecosystem.
Developed product and content architecture, responsive layouts, design-system patterns, and motion implementation.
Implemented accessibility improvements, SEO support, and verified waitlist infrastructure using Supabase, Resend, and Cloudflare Turnstile.
challenges: The original product story did not clearly communicate what TekGlove was or how its technology worked.
Six products needed to feel distinct while remaining visibly connected to one core platform.
Complex concepts involving sensors, biometrics, gestures, artificial intelligence, and connected hardware had to remain understandable to a broad audience.
The website needed to support product renders that would become available gradually without making incomplete pages feel unfinished.
The existing external waitlist journey did not belong to TekGlove and had to be replaced with a secure, brand-specific system.
approach: Reframed TekGlove around the hand as a rich source of interpretable data.
Established the Smart Dorsal Sensor as the technology powering the wider product ecosystem.
Created a shared product-page structure that can scale consistently across all six gloves.
Developed individual accent-colour systems to distinguish each product without weakening the TekGlove identity.
Used restrained motion, product imagery, interactive diagrams, and textured surfaces to make technical storytelling more engaging.
Built a verified waitlist flow using Supabase, Resend, and Cloudflare Turnstile, including product-interest capture and glove-specific audience segmentation.
Improved metadata, accessibility, responsive behaviour, navigation, validation, and component architecture across the website.
outcome: The completed experience presents TekGlove as a coherent wearable technology platform rather than a collection of unrelated concepts.
Visitors can understand how one core sensor architecture supports six products across multiple industries.
Each priority product now has a dedicated, scalable storytelling experience and its own recognisable visual identity.
TekGlove can securely capture verified audience interest and organise subscribers according to the products they want to hear about.
caseStudy.pullQuote: The hand is not just an interface. It is a source of data.
